RB-415: HIGH API LATENCY
========================

Service:        public-api (k8s namespace: api)
Severity:       SEV-2
Owner:          API Platform team
Last reviewed:  2026-09-21


1. SYMPTOMS
-----------

  * Alert ApiLatencyP99High fires: p99 latency above 800 ms for 5 minutes.
  * Error budget burn rate above 2x on the "api-availability" SLO.
  * Customers report timeouts on POST /v2/orders.


2. LATENCY TARGETS
------------------

  +-------------------+---------+---------+-----------+
  | Endpoint          | p50     | p99     | Timeout   |
  +-------------------+---------+---------+-----------+
  | GET  /v2/orders   | 40 ms   | 300 ms  | 2 s       |
  | POST /v2/orders   | 90 ms   | 800 ms  | 5 s       |
  | GET  /v2/search   | 120 ms  | 1200 ms | 5 s       |
  +-------------------+---------+---------+-----------+


3. DIAGNOSIS
------------

3.1 Is it one pod or all of them?

    kubectl -n api top pods --sort-by=cpu
    kubectl -n api get hpa public-api

  If only one pod is slow, delete it and let the deployment replace it:

    kubectl -n api delete pod <POD_NAME>

3.2 Is a dependency slow?

  Check the downstream latency panel in the "public-api / dependencies"
  Grafana dashboard. The usual suspects, in order:

    1. orders-db (see RB-204 if the primary is down)
    2. redis-cache (hit ratio below 85% means a cold cache)
    3. search-service


4. REMEDIATION
--------------

  1. If CPU is above 80% on all pods, scale out:
       kubectl -n api scale deployment public-api --replicas=12
  2. If a deploy happened in the last hour, roll it back:
       kubectl -n api rollout undo deployment public-api
  3. If redis hit ratio is low, warm the cache:
       kubectl -n api create job warm-cache --from=cronjob/cache-warmer

  WARNING: do not raise the HPA maxReplicas above 20; orders-db allows
  at most 400 connections through pgbouncer.


5. ESCALATION
-------------

  L1  On-call SRE              #ops-oncall
  L2  API Platform on-call     PagerDuty: api-platform
  L3  Engineering manager      only for SEV-1 or more than 1 hour of impact
